subject: DATE-OF-INTEGER function
notes: SURVIVES REVIEW. Independently re-verified rather than inherited. Symbols confirmed literally present: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` at CobolExpressions.g4, `public static class IntrinsicCatalog`, and `BindIntrinsicArgs` in IntrinsicBinder.cs; the catalog row is `Add(new("DATE-OF-INTEGER", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "DateOfInteger", ...))` — Fixed 1..1, matching the single parenthesized argument-1 of §15.22.2. Positive forms RAN clean: `FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(143951)`, `FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER ( 143951 )` (separator spaces), an identifier operand, an arithmetic-expression operand `(A + B)`, a numeric-edited operand, and the call as an EVALUATE subject and in an IF condition. Negative direction RAN: two arguments gives 'error COBOL1504: FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)'; the paren-less form is caught by the same arity arm ('0 given'), so the grammar's optional argument-list parenthesis does not let the format through. Identical acceptance under --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 (all four print 16010101 for the epoch case). Test-ref re-verified ON DISK at tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 265; its helper `AssertSpec` compiles and compares to a hand-written expectation with NO oracle involved (`AssertSameAsLegacy` is a different helper this method does not call), so it is genuinely spec-derived and it does compile the §15.22.2 form. Caveat, not a defect: the test pins only the POSITIVE form; the arity rejection is unpinned by any checked-in spec-derived test.
